subject: Re: nimbleCode: ragged array or similar data structure for random variables?

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: nimbleCode: ragged array or similar data structure for random variables?
parts:
Gregory, thanks for your email, and your use of NIMBLE.  If I'm not mistaken, your code is nearly spot-on for doing this (with a single ragged array structure).  Slightly modified code appears below.  The only minor disadvantage I can imagine here, is that the ragged array structure will result in the allocation of some unnecessary memory (specifically: the unused elements of those "rows" aside from the row of complete length.  If this memory is a legitimate concern, then we could discuss other approaches.

Anyway, this runs fine for me, and hopefully answers your question:


library(nimble)

m <- 5
ns <- c(1, 5, 10, 20, 3)       ## number of elements in each of the 'm' groups

poisCode <- nimbleCode({
    ##
    ## Parameters with priors
    for (cell in 1:m) {
        lambda[cell] ~ dunif(0, 5000)
    }
    ##
    ## The data and its probability distributions
    for (cell in 1:m) {
        for (sample in 1:ns[cell]) {   ## changed index to 'cell', rather than 'm'
            x[sample, cell] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[cell])
        }
    }
})

x <- array(0, c(max(ns), m))   ## your actual data here

constants <- list(m = m, ns = ns)
data <- list(x = x)
inits <- list(lambda = rep(1, m))

Rmodel <- nimbleModel(poisCode, constants, data, inits)

Rmodel$calculate()
## -81.58597   ## looks good, model is fully initialized




On Sun, Oct 20, 2019 at 3:04 AM Gregory Penn <gregor...@gmail.com> wrote:
First day using NIMBLE, so I apologize if this is clearly documented somewhere and I haven't found it.

I have a set of random variables (the data) that are grouped by a shared parameter and vary in number between groups. What's the best way to code that within nimbleCode?

Here's what I've tried. The model is just supposed to estimate m independent Poisson distributions as a step toward a more complex model.

poisCode <- nimbleCode({

  # Parameters with priors
  for (cell in 1:m) {
    lambda[cell] ~ dunif(0, 5000)
  }

  # The data and its probability distributions
  for (cell in 1:m) {
    for (sample in 1:ns[m]) {
      x[[cell]][sample] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[cell])
      # x[sample, cell] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[cell])
    }
  }

})


The commented line of code works for special cases where the number of samples in each cell is the same. No problem there.
The line above it is my attempt to store the samples in a ragged array, a list of vectors of unequal length. That fails as follows:

poisModel <- nimbleModel(poisCode,
                         constants = list(ns = ns, m = m),
                         inits = list(lambda = lambda_init))
# defining model...
# Error in genReplacementsAndCodeRecurse(x, constAndIndexNames, nimbleFunctionNames,  :
# Error, R function "[[" has non-replaceable node values as arguments.  Must be a nimble function.

I found a page in the manual with a section "more on indexing" from which this looked like a possibility

x[cell[sample]] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[cell])

but I couldn't figure out what the corresponding data structure would be and if failed with

# defining model...
# Error in if (any(sapply(varInfo, function(x) length(x$mins) && length(x$maxs) &&  :
#   missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

So what's the best way to do this?

Thanks in advance,
Gregory

messages.subject: Re: nimbleCode: ragged array or similar data structure for random variables?
parts:
Hi Gregory, an alternative is to take the ragged array and string it out into a long vector containing all the elements. Then have 'cell' be a vector of the same length indicating the cell of each observation, something like:

for(i in 1:n)
  x[i] ~ dpois(lambda = lambda[cell[i]]

Chris
